## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded, but concerns the earlier source and does not supply any passage from the DOI-associated paper. It does not establish the named certificate.
- claim-2: Correctly identifies the earlier paper, but is irrelevant to ingesting and indexing the full text associated with DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\).
- claim-3: The conclusion matches the exhibited evidence gap, but its status is unsupported rather than proved: no DOI-associated full text, integrity record, or exhaustive indexed passage audit was supplied. The certificate remains unestablished.

## Repair certificates
- [source-refresh] Ingest a full-text artifact whose bibliographic page explicitly records DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); record its stable artifact identifier and cryptographic digest; then provide exact page-and-line-indexed passages containing (i) the complete main theorem, (ii) all coefficient-ring hypotheses and definitions of \(J_v\) and \(A_+\), and (iii) every occurrence or equivalent formulation of \(J_v/A_+J_v\), including any rank, basis, freeness, torsion, parameter, or boundary-case statements. Include a reproducible exhaustive text-search index covering \(J_v\), \(A_+\), “indecomposable,” “quotient,” and the paper’s equivalent notation.

## Required revisions
- Replace the audit of older sources with the required DOI-associated full-text artifact and exact indexed quotations.
- Explicitly distinguish statements quoted from the paper from conclusions inferred from them.
- Conclude only whether this source-ingestion certificate is established; make no parent-theorem claim.
